answer: Each agent identity can hold a hardware anchor: a chip fuses a one-time secret into a kernel-protected register at manufacture, so one device cannot mint a second identity without destroying the first. Registration verifies a remote attestation quote against the vendor's fuse map, and cloned software keys fail that quote. Taking a vote therefore costs real silicon per seat, a physical supply limit rather than a scripted loop. A jade credential is issued only after a second, independent attestation, which keeps cheap key-copies out of governance.
